text: Finding the real cause starts by reproducing the gap on command, then checking whether it happens at a different quarter boundary too — which rules out a one-time data mistake and points at the formula's own logic.

An isolation formula, summing only orders placed on October 1st, 2013 exactly, tests the real suspect directly. If that number matches the size of the gap, that's the mechanism caught in the act, not a guess.

The bug is an inclusive upper bound. Less than or equal to October 1st includes October 1st — but October 1st is the first day of Q4, not the last day of Q3. One character, changing less-than-or-equal to just less-than, is the entire fix.

Power BI and Tableau were never vulnerable to this, because both filter through a calendar dimension where every day belongs to exactly one quarter, with no boundary ambiguity for a human to get wrong. Next lesson applies the fix and re-validates all three deliverables.
